description.narrative: Efficiency of the road sector improved
Travel time between Karshi and Kitab decreased to 97 minutes Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: No civil works contractors mobilized. Please see status above. Data Source: SCR completion report

Annual average daily traffic on the Karshi-Kitab road in Kashkadarya increased to about 14,000 by 2022 Achievement: 0 Progress/Status: On 25 January 2021, ADB received the Borrower's request to cancel the loan funds under L3481-UZB. The letter stated that (i) the ongoing COVID-19 pandemic inflicted substantial shocks for the economy of the Republic of Uzbekistan and made the government borrow additional funds to address COVID-19 and other shocks in 2020, (ii) the government reassessed its public investment priorities in light of limited borrowing headroom, and (iii) although the subject road project remains a priority for the government, due to the increased borrowing for other investments, the government decided to postpone construction of the road. Consequently, ADB cancelled $193.45 million and $3.92 million effective 11 March 2021 and 13 April 2021, respectively. The loan account is financially closed effective 13 April 2021.
The project experienced substantial procurement delays owing to temporary suspension of activities in 2017 due to government transition, change of EA, revision of design, feasibility study and cost estimates and delay in signing of contracts due to, at first, issues on taxes and duties on temporary importation of equipment. When the issues on taxes and duties were resolved, the next cause of delay in contract signing was due to the government's change of priorities in the road sector. The notification of contract award to both contractors for Lots 1 and 2 were issued on 20 December 2019. Eventually, the EA issued the contract termination notice to the two winning bidders for the two lots and to the construction supervision consultant on 24 March 2021. Data Source: Periodic classified traffic counts (collected by Uzavtoyul)

ADB cancelled the loan proceeds in two tranches: on 11 March 2021 and 13 April 2021. The EA issued the contract termination notice to the two winning bidders for the two lots and to the construction supervision consultant on 24 March 2021. The loan account is financially closed effective 13 April 2021.
Bidding history: • As of October 2020, no official feedback received since CWTC sent a letter in mid-July to CR informing of the negative consequences that would arise from the loan cancellation. • The contracts have not been signed yet, at first, due to issues on taxes and duties on temporary importation of equipment and then, due to government's change in priorities for road sector. Currently, the matter is being resolved with the concerned agencies. • Notification of award to both contracts were issued in December 2019 (20 December 2019 for Lot 1, and 19 December 2019 for Lot 2). • Price bids were opened on 9 July 2019. ADB gave no objection to the FBER and award of contract on 15 Nov 2019 for Lot 1 and on 27 November 2019 for Lot 2. • The TBER was submitted to ADB on 17 April 2019. ADB no objection to the TBER issued on 2 July 2019. • The IFB for the procurement of two lots (total 77 km): (i) Lot 1: Reconstruction of 4P-79 Road from Km28 to Km64 and 4K319 Road from Km 18 to Km30 (48km); and (ii) Lot-2: Reconstruction of M-39 Road from Km 1144 to Km 1173 (29km) was advertised on 16 October 2018. Bids were opened on 15 January 2019.
The two ongoing road projects in UZB experienced delays due to government transition, suspension of procurement, revisiting of design, feasibility study, and cost estimates. And since issuance of letters of acceptance to the winning bidders in December 2019, delay in signing the contracts. Data Source: SCR completion report
